elements.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: Section 5.3(d) makes "an Affiliate of the Depositor to whom the Depositor has assigned this Agreement" the successor Depositor, and the retained opening of Section 10.2(a) ("Except as stated in Sections 5.3 and 7.4") keeps that route outside the consent requirement. The redline does not disturb the Section 5.3 exception.

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
elements.evidence: Section 5.3 covers any Person "(a) into which the Depositor is merged or consolidated, (b) resulting from a merger or consolidation to which the Depositor is a party, (c) succeeding to the Depositor's business", and Section 10.2(a) still excepts Section 5.3 from the consent list; "succeeding to the Depositor's business" carries the substantially-all-assets case.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: Operation 1 strikes "7.6" from the exception list and adds "and, for the Servicer, the Issuer" to the required consents, so Section 10.2(a) now reads that the Agreement "may not be assigned by ... the Servicer without the consent of ... and, for the Servicer, the Issuer". The remaining Section 7.4 exception is the involuntary Successor Servicer appointment mechanic, not a Servicer-elected transfer, so it does not undercut the element. Section 7.6 survives only as a successorship-consequence provision and no longer confers a consent-free Affiliate transfer.

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Added language: "and, for the Servicer, the Issuer, whose consent will not be unreasonably withheld." The qualifier attaches to the Customer-side (Issuer) consent, which is what the element requires; the pre-existing third-party trustee/Noteholder consents are untouched.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: New free-standing sentence: "The Servicer may not assign this Agreement to a competitor of the Issuer or the Depositor." It is unconditional and covers both Customer-side entities.

elements.element: Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
elements.evidence: Section 7.1 (retained): "The Servicer will not resign as Servicer under this Agreement unless it determines it is legally unable to perform its obligations under this Agreement." No cited provision gives Cellco a termination, resignation or re-pricing right on a Depositor/Issuer change of control, and the redline adds none.

elements.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
elements.evidence: After operation 1 removed Section 7.6 from the Section 10.2(a) carve-out, a Servicer merger/succession transfer is no longer permitted of right: it now requires Owner Trustee, Indenture Trustee, Certificateholder, 66-2/3% Controlling Class Noteholder and Issuer consent. The Vendor leg of a mutual free successor right therefore does not exist in the rendered text (deliberately, since the proposal targets the preferred level).

elements.element: A successor assignment requires written notice.
elements.evidence: Sections 5.3 and 7.6 each require, within fifteen (15) Business Days, delivery to the Issuer, Owner Trustee and Indenture Trustee of an Officer's Certificate and Opinion of Counsel and notification of the Rating Agencies \u2013 written notice mechanics that survive the redline.

Section 5.3(d) is retained and remains excepted from Section 10.2(a), so the Depositor may still assign to its own Affiliate with no consent. Per the ASSIGN fallback boundary, a retained no-consent non-successor (affiliate) exception defeats this element, even though it runs in Customer's favour.

elements.element: Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The reasonableness qualifier was added only to the Issuer's consent for Servicer assignments ("for the Servicer, the Issuer, whose consent will not be unreasonably withheld"). The Owner Trustee, Indenture Trustee, Certificateholder and 66-2/3% Noteholder consents \u2013 and every consent applicable to a Depositor assignment \u2013 remain unqualified.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: all six preferred elements are met in operative language. The outbound leg was already compliant (Section 5.3 affiliate/successor route excepted from Section 10.2(a); Section 7.1 bars Servicer resignation absent legal inability), and the three edits cure the inbound leg (Issuer consent, reasonableness standard, competitor bar) and close the Section 7.6 consent-free Affiliate transfer.

The fallback checklist is not satisfied (successor right is no longer mutual; the Section 5.3 affiliate carve-out remains a no-consent non-successor exception; the reasonableness standard is confined to the Issuer's consent for Servicer assignments). That is immaterial to completeness because the preferred level is fully met, and the "deviation" finding status is correct \u2013 in the original text the Section 7.6 Affiliate carve-out, absence of any Issuer consent right and absence of a competitor bar failed the fallback on material terms.

Minimality holds. Three targeted operations, each traceable to a selected element: striking "7.6" from the Section 10.2(a) exception list (needed for "Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent"), inserting the Issuer's consent with the not-unreasonably-withheld qualifier (elements 3 and 4), and one short competitor-bar sentence (element 5). No survival tail, no procedure, no notice period, no expense language, no deletion of favourable retained text: Sections 5.3, 7.1, 7.4 and the existing trustee/Noteholder consents are all preserved verbatim.

Intent is preserved. The Section 10.2(a) cross-references to Sections 5.3 and 7.4 still resolve, Section 7.6 remains a live successorship-consequence provision (it defines who becomes successor once a permitted merger/succession/assignment occurs) rather than a standing consent-free permission, so no dangling reference or contradictory retained sentence is created. The Section 7.4 Successor Servicer mechanics and the Section 6.4 delegation regime are untouched.

Residual points for the drafter (not defects requiring repair, but worth a conforming tweak): (i) because Section 7.6 is no longer excepted, a Cellco merger or consolidation now triggers the full 66-2/3% Controlling Class consent \u2013 if that is broader than intended, add an express successor-only carve-back rather than reinstating the Affiliate limb; (ii) consider conforming Section 7.6's opening words to "Subject to Section 10.2(a)" to remove any argument that it self-authorises an Affiliate assignment; (iii) the added competitor bar has no defined-term anchor for "competitor" \u2013 acceptable as a plain-meaning standard, but a definition would remove interpretive risk.
